correctness.rationale: For the unrestricted uniform ordered pair, alternating paths have exponential weights 1 for odd size and 1/2 per endpoint class for even size; even graph cycles have weight 1/k including k=2. Removing an ordered tuple of specified components leaves the coefficient ratio b_{n−s}/b_n. Lugo's positive coefficient asymptotic yields the uniform e^{-s/√n}(1+o(1)) ratio for s=O(√n log n), by the square-root expansion and the uniform prefactor. For s≤n/2 the ratio is bounded by C e^{-s/√n}; for s>n/2 even multiplying the exponentially small bound by a fixed polynomial in n does not affect factorial moment sums. Disjoint marked-window mixed factorial moments factorize, and odd/even lattice sums each have half the total weight, giving the three Poisson intensities. The first-moment upper-tail bound gives tightness at the top, the cycle weight 1/k makes large alternating cycles negligible, and the equal-size ordered-path pair bound is O(n^{-1/2}) above each fixed low height cutoff. Since a path yields one permutation cycle of its own size, while an even graph cycle gives two of half its size, this establishes the maximum and top mark conclusions. An independently implemented bounded check covered 60,397 ordered pairs through n=7 and verified 106 exact marked component/coefficient identities; the 60,528 in the frozen narrative counts assertions in its supplied script, not pairs.
residual_risks: No explicit rate for the full marked process or any assertion about the fixed-point-conditioned model; bounded enumeration does not certify the infinite limit.

evidence: Panagiotou–Ramzews gives Gumbel for this expansive assembly. Its saddle after undoing the tilt is exp(−η_n) with η_n=n^{-1/2}+O(n^{-1}); here zC′(z)=η^{-2}+O(η^{-1}) and C(z)=η^{-1}+O(log(1/η)), with C(z)=log B(z). Theorem 1.2's threshold is thus √n(log√n+x)+o(√n).
Equations (3.27)–(3.28) supply moving-window joint occupancy and uniform upper bounds, not just a marginal limit for the maximum.
Lugo's and Roberts–Vivaldi's fixed-point-conditioned formulas by themselves do not give this unrestricted marked PPP.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The expansive theorem and its verified estimates cover this special case and much more. The fixed-point-conditioned results are relevant comparators, not the basis of the failure.

evidence: For each fixed number r of distinct occupied sizes in bounded extreme windows, (3.27) gives their joint probability as (1+o(1))∏ c_k exp(−η_n k) after undoing the tilt. The bounded windows are O(√n) wide, hence o of the lower threshold. One may sum over any specified parity and any disjoint windows, not just over consecutive sizes.

Summing those products gives the mixed Poisson factorial moments of occupied-size counts, with lattice weights 1/2 for odd and 1/2 for even. Diagonals in the product sums vanish since every extreme site has weight O(n^{-1/2}). Actual multiple components of the same size vanish in probability by the assembly second factorial identity and the coefficient bound: the sum of squared extreme-site weights is O(n^{-1/2}). The uniform upper bound controls the height tail beyond a fixed upper cutoff.

Conditional on the sizes, component types are independent allocations. At odd sizes all components are paths of type O; at even sizes the unnormalized weights are 1/2, 1/2 and 1/k for S, T and graph cycles. Summing cycle expectations gives O(1/(√n log n)); the other two allocations are equiprobable and give the independent marked intensities 1/4 each. The unique top mark and height distribution and the product-cycle interpretation then follow.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: This is a direct specialization of the prior moving-window estimates plus already known type weights, not an attempt to infer microscopic parity just from a continuous unmarked PPP. It covers the whole marked point-process conclusion as well as the maximum.

evidence: The pair of involutions is a labelled assembly with connected weights c_k=1+1_{k even}/k and occupation-vector law proportional to ∏_k c_k^{N_k}/N_k! on ∑kN_k=n.

Replacing c_k with ρ^{-k}c_k for any fixed 0<ρ<1 multiplies the occupation weight by the same ρ^{-n} for all vectors. It gives precisely the expansive α=1, radius ρ, labelled C-set case of their theorem, with slowly varying h(k)=c_k→1.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Taking the original radius as 1 would obscure that the cited labelled case applies: the harmless exponential tilt moves the radius to ρ with no change of the conditioned model or of the color probabilities.

originality.rationale: The finding is correct but already follows from the published largest-cluster and discrete joint extreme-occupancy estimates of Panagiotou–Ramzews (2022), applied to the Lugo assembly, followed by exact conditional coloring. This is not merely prior coverage of a scalar Gumbel law: their estimates apply to arbitrary distinct sizes in the moving extreme window, which retains the parity information. They give the Poisson joint law for counts on disjoint windows intersected with odd and even sites; the remaining subdivision is independent thinning with known weights. No substantive distinct claim survives in the bound finding.
residual_risks: The primary expansive paper need not state these specific involution labels; the implication uses its exact lattice occupancy estimates and the independent Lugo component classification. No priority is inferred from the same-date Resultary hits.

value.rationale: The maximum period is a meaningful observable, and the specialization is correct. But the bound claim adds only a standard application of published local extreme-assembly estimates, a parity Riemann sum and known independent type allocation. It gives no new extremal mechanism, quantitative control beyond what supports that specialization, or independent geometric/dynamical conclusion not accessible from those inputs. The tie and graph-cycle bounds are routine consequences of the same coefficient estimates. No genuinely separate valuable remainder within the assigned claim was established, so no repair is submitted.
residual_risks: This does not say longest reversible periods are unimportant, only that this bound claim does not advance their analysis beyond applying existing results.
